versions.rationale: One patch increment for a focused security-contract clarification; no shipped executable code or dependency changed.

files.attribution: Assignment package was clean. Only the three owned package files changed. All generated keys/certificates are synthetic OS-temp fixtures, not user credentials; no review files shipped.

changes.change: Replaces universal certificate-chain wording with profile-defined proof and trust requirements, retaining PKI chain/expected-peer checks and restricting the registered-certificate alternative to explicitly supported profiles.
changes.consequence: An adequate self-signed OAuth mTLS method can be preserved without introducing a trust-all fallback.

changes.change: Distinguishes RFC 8705 PKI and registered self-signed client authentication; requires trusted registration, TLS possession and client binding, with same-subject/header and wrong-profile controls.
changes.consequence: Matching a subject or presenting a copied certificate cannot confer authority; the exception cannot silently weaken other PKI/SPIFFE/HTTPS boundaries.
Coordinator can publish the changed package integrity under a new version.

criteria: Actual reachable path and identity evidence at the protected effect.
Separate workload, user, actor, tenant and principal kind/namespace.
Profile-specific issuer/audience/certificate semantics, token purpose and binding.
Delegation, proxy assertions and client-selected metadata trust boundaries.
Credential/policy lifecycle and warm/cold/expired/revoked cache/connection states.

correctedFinding.evidence: RFC 8705 section 2.2 expressly uses registered client certificates plus TLS possession without chain validation; section 2.1 requires a valid chain and configured subject for PKI. The initial unconditional chain instruction failed to preserve that supported distinction.
correctedFinding.impact: Could incorrectly reject an existing valid mechanism or encourage an improvised global verification exception.

investigatedWithoutExpansion: Existing generic all-decision-input cache rule, expiry/failure table and warm-cache principal-kind adversarial case were preserved rather than expanded into another generic checklist.
Authentication versus certificate-bound-token validation remains explicitly separate; this change adds no token endpoint, IdP or cryptography implementation.

preserved: Architecture and verification-contract role; no mandatory mesh, SPIFFE, OAuth or identity-platform migration.
Workload/subject/actor/tenant separation and same-issuer same-subject user/client collision protection.
Trusted issuer/key source selection, token-purpose profile separation, scope/audience and optional specialist handoffs.
All reachable entry paths, proxy termination/header stripping/bypass protection and effect-owner authorization.
TOCTOU protection, trusted context construction, executor context caveats and async fact-versus-command authority.
Delegation current actor versus history, exchange revocation limitations and certificate-bound-token distinctions.
Rotation overlap versus compromise, bounded caches, expiry and unknown-state failure behavior, long-lived connection coverage.
Existing conceptual policy example and hostile-test table; no capability intentionally removed.

structuredWalkthroughs.result: Supported registration binding and TLS possession permit A; a chain mandate is unnecessary for this profile, while same-name/header and wrong-client controls remain denied.
Changing only selected method requires the trusted PKI chain and registered subject; A cannot use registration to bypass it, and C becomes the positive credential.

behavioralEvaluations.measuredImprovement: Not measured. Executed cryptographic transport/policy fixtures support the corrected contract; no matched agent comparison was performed.

sources.supports: PKI chain plus registered subject versus self-signed TLS certificate matching against trusted client registration, with proof of possession and claimed-client binding.
Existing separation of OAuth mTLS authentication and certificate-bound tokens; protected resource compares the presented certificate with token binding.
Existing client/user subject semantics, required client_id claim, and access-token profile validation.
Existing current actor versus nested actor-history distinction.
Existing introspection cache trade-off and expiration bound.
Existing audience/privilege restrictions, sender constraints, proxy and client-impersonation threat distinctions.
Fixture requestCert, CA authorization/rejection behavior, peer-certificate access and HTTPS server-name verification inputs.

limitations: The seven runtime cases are technical fixture executions, not independent agent evaluations or production security guarantees.
No OAuth provider, Spring implementation, real token issuance, token signature validation or authorization-server registration API was exercised.
TLS uses fresh loopback connections; no session resumption, rotation, revocation, certificate expiry, compromised-key withdrawal or proxy network reachability was tested.
The fixture's PKI subject comparison is intentionally narrow to its synthetic CN and is not a reusable implementation of provider distinguished-name matching.

The registered-profile fixture admits self-signed certificates at the TLS transport layer only to require exact trusted registration before its effect. It is test evidence, not a recommendation to disable verification on arbitrary production listeners.
Two-day synthetic certificate validity limits direct artifact replay; generation instructions are retained for a fresh isolated replay.
No benchmark or measured quality gain. Global checks are coordinator-owned.

twoCases.prerequisites: Load service-identity-and-trust and its routed protocol reference. These are sanitized architecture fixtures. For an independent evaluation, expose only taskInput and optional public certificate metadata, not evaluator criteria or probe-results.json. No production identity system, live credentials or provider implementation is needed.

taskInput.task: Review whether payments can authenticate with certificate-A under the effective client configuration and specify the required checks and negative controls. A reviewer proposes requiring a CA chain for all methods; another proposes accepting any certificate with CN=payments. Resolve the contract from the selected method, preserve already adequate mechanisms, and describe the narrow correction or no change. Do not change the provider, disable server authentication, broaden another listener or assume certificate-bound access tokens are enabled.

files.provider-capabilities.md: The deployed OAuth provider supports RFC 8705 tls_client_auth and self_signed_tls_client_auth. The selected per-client method governs authentication. Clients reach the provider's authenticated HTTPS token endpoint directly; no forwarded certificate header is an identity source. Server authentication remains enabled. The trusted client record below was provisioned by the approved administrator.
files.effect-contract.md: Successful authentication may enter the client's separately authorized token-issuance flow. Authentication failures must not issue a token or cause a protected effect. Same subject text is not evidence that two certificates or keys are equal. Record which later authorization, token binding and provider behavior remain outside this review.
files.effective-client.yaml:
client_id: payments
token_endpoint_auth_method: self_signed_tls_client_auth
registered_certificates: [certificate-A]
tls_client_auth_subject_dn: CN=payments
trusted_pki_roots: [fixture-CA]

evaluatorExpectations.decisiveEvidence: The effective method selects registered-certificate authentication and the trusted record includes certificate-A, whose possession is proven in TLS.
evaluatorExpectations.acceptableOutcome: Retain A under this explicitly supported profile without inventing a CA-chain prerequisite. Preserve exact certificate-to-client registration binding, private-key proof, HTTPS server validation and separate authorization.
requiredNegativeControls: B with the same CN and a different unregistered certificate cannot authenticate payments.
A used for another unregistered client_id must fail.
A certificate string/header without TLS possession must fail.
C is not acceptable under this method merely because its chain and subject are valid.
failureConditions: Requires migration to PKI solely because A is self-signed.
Treats subject equality or a forwarded string as proof of identity.
Turns the exception into general trust-all TLS or weakens the server certificate check.
Claims successful client authentication binds every resulting bearer token automatically.

evaluatorExpectations.decisiveEvidence: The active method requires PKI validation. A does not chain to the configured root; its stored registration entry is not permission to fall back to another authentication method.
evaluatorExpectations.acceptableOutcome: Reject A under the selected PKI contract. C is the positive control when its trusted chain, registered subject and TLS possession all verify. If changing method is desired, make that an explicit reviewed contract change, not fallback-on-failure behavior.
requiredNegativeControls: A and B must not cause issuance/effects under PKI merely because CN matches.
A's presence in another credential record must not bypass selected profile checks.
Wrong subject on an otherwise trusted chain must be denied in provider verification.
failureConditions: Accepts A solely because it appears in the registration while PKI is selected.

Accepts any CA-issued subject without the configured client binding.
